newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arafat starts talks with France's Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Arafat starts talks with France's Chirac.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat met French President Jacques Chirac on Friday to brief him on the outcome of the Middle East summit in Washington this week.
Chirac came out to greet Arafat on the steps of the Elysee palace as the presidential guard paid him honours usually reserved for heads of state.
The Palestinian president arrived from Italy, where he had met Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini. He was expected to leave France later on Friday night.

France sniped at Washington for the scant results of the two-day Middle East summit and said Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak should play a major role in trying to revive the Israeli-Palestinian peace process.

"A meeting prepared in other conditions would have allowed concrete results," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said of the emergency summit at the White House that ended with no breakthroughs apart from a deal to keep talking.
Fifty-eight Arabs and 15 Jews have died in fighting since last week.
"The positions are still very far apart," Rummelhardt told reporters hours before Arafat's arrival to brief Chirac on the results of his meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
France had previously faulted U.S. President Bill Clinton for failing to invite European leaders to the White House meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Chirac's own position as possible power-broker or mediator was bolstered on Thursday when he hosted a meeting between the presidents of Bosnia and rump Yugoslavia who agreed to open diplomatic relations and take other confidence-building steps after a four-year war.
Chirac, speaking earlier in the day in Naples, Italy said European Union leaders were expected to call at their summit on Saturday for an active role in reviving the Middle East peace process.
Chirac said France and Italy had agreed at bilateral talks to ask their partners to issue the call at the Dublin meeting, adding: "I believe that everyone will agree with it."
The statement would affirm "the desire of Europe to take part in relaunching the peace process", Chirac told a joint news conference with the Italian prime minister.

The French foreign ministry spokesman earlier said, "France hails the efforts of the parties concerned to revive the peace process." Israelis and Palestinians have agreed to hold new talks at the Erez crossing between Gaza and Israel from Sunday.
He said it was essential for the Erez talks to lead quickly to results in implementing the existing Middle East peace accords.
